scoreboard.footnote: Total tokens (input + output + cache read + cache write), median of 3 runs per side; Headroom, Caveman, Config, CLI vs MCP = task 1 (small edit); Headroom (long answer), Caveman (long answer) = task 6 (written code review, no edits); Headroom (long chat), Caveman (long chat) = task 7 (6-message conversation in one session).  Headroom = traffic routed through headroom proxy (Bedrock passthrough to the local gateway), --mode token, --no-optimize vs optimizing.  * OFF and ON ranges overlap — within run-to-run noise.

findings.head: Config: biggest win in our run
findings.body: Task 1, n=3: 146,660–148,224 → 111,195–111,746 tokens, turns 4 → 3. Facilitator run — yours may vary.

findings.head: Caveman: shorter answers…
findings.body: …but total tokens +7%: its ruleset is extra context on every turn.

findings.head: Caveman in a long chat
findings.body: Tokens +5%: output is only 0.7% of a long chat's tokens.

findings.head: Long chats live on the prompt cache
findings.body: Reads bill at 1/10 of input: $0.55 per 6-message chat cached vs $2.49 uncached (−78%), Sonnet list price. Keep the prefix stable; compact, don't restart.

findings.head: CLI vs MCP: within noise
findings.body: Both MCP servers connected, yet their schemas didn't move the total on this task.

findings.head: Headroom: the chat cost more
findings.body: edit 0%*, review −1%*, chat +13% (* = noise). Proxy compressed 43,790 tokens over 85 requests it inspected.
